text:
maria: FYI customers reporting p95/p99 spike on /v1/generate starting ~08:10 UTC. graph shows p95 from 110ms -> 420ms, p99 from 280ms -> 1.8s. noticed after the 07:50 kernel-chooser rollout. :frowning_face:

sam: alerted by synthetic tests?

maria: yep, synthetic and support tickets. Synthetic from eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Link to grafana: https://grafana.internal/redwood/r/latency?panel=75 (paste).

oncall-bot: INCIDENT ALERT: High latency on hosted-api /v1/generate (p95>400ms) - incident created id INC-20260315-427

ryan: I see a cluster of slow tails on the serving nodes that picked kernel variant v2.3.2. Traces show model inference spans elongated, queue wait increased.

alex: Could be batching behavior changed after the kernel selector update. Any recent changes to batching config or prefix caching?

maria: We rolled kernel-chooser 07:45 with a heuristic that prefers fused attention for seq_len>512. Most traffic is seq_len~300, so it should have chosen previous kernels. But selector telemetry shows many misclassifications for model redwood-x-3b.

sam: Repro steps I ran: curl -X POST host:/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-x-3b","input":"<long prompt ~350 tokens>"}' -H "Authorization: Bearer ..." -> p95 ~600ms locally hit us-west nodes. If I force model_variant=classic-kernel it drops to 120ms.

jane-support: A few paying customers reported UI lag and timeouts (timeouts set to 2s), multiple 504s. Billing impact potential if we miss SLOs.

maria: Immediate mitigations applied: 1) rolled back kernel-chooser to previous 07:30 canary on all serving clusters (rollback-id rc-07-30-chooser) 2) enabled emergency circuit-breaker rule for /v1/generate on hosted tier to limit concurrency per-client to 8 3) created routing fallback to model redwood-x-3b-quant for non-SLA customers in eu-west-1.

sam: Nice. Rollback confirmation: all nodes back to kernel v2.2.9. Metrics showing p95 starting to decrease now.

ryan: Additional short-term play: reduce autoscaling target cpu to 60% -> adds a couple instances to reduce queueing. Also bumped batch_size max from 40 -> 24 to avoid long batching tails.

alex: We should also surface a graceful 429 with Retry-After for clients hitting concurrency limit. People will see throttles but better than 504s.

maria: Agreed. I pushed a quick gateway rule: on circuit-breaker tripped -> return 429 with header Retry-After: 5. Rolling out now.

jane-support: Noted. I updated the support triage doc and messaged top customers. Will offer to switch them to dedicated capacity if they want guaranteed latency.

sam: Root cause hypothesis: kernel-chooser misprediction + batch size increase caused request coalescing into larger batches for some request shapes, increasing tail latency. Combine that with underprovisioned pool for a recent traffic spike from a marketing campaign.

ryan: Evidence: traces show large batch assembly times on nodes that selected fused kernel, CPU waits spiked, SLOs missed only for seq_len in 280-400 window.

maria: Next steps (short term):
- keep rollback until we have a validated kernel selection metric set
- keep circuit-breaker active for next 24h
- ramp down batch_size max to 16 for hosted (safe default)
- enable 429 Retry-After header
- keep fallback routing to quant model for non-SLA customers in eu-west and us-west

sam: Next steps (medium term):
- add kernel-selector telemetry: per-model confusion matrix + per-seqlen hit-rate, ship dashboard and alert when mismatch >1%
- implement ci test that runs sampling of real request shapes against kernel-chooser in staging before rollout
- automatic rollback policy if p95 increases >20% within 30m of rollout

alex: Also add SLO guardrails to API gateway:
- soft rate limit per-API-key with exponential backoff headers
- circuit-breaker state persisted across restarts so it doesn't flip-flop
- fallback routing policy that prefers cheaper/quantized model variants when latency thresholds breached

jane-support: For customers impacted, recommended mitigation in support response: 1) retry with smaller inputs 2) use model_variant=quant or model_variant=classic-kernel 3) request a temporary rate limit increase to Dedicated if they need throughput.

ryan: I pushed a quick patch to the autoscaler: ignore short spikes < 2m when deciding scale-down, prevents thrash. Rolling to canary.

maria: Observability tasks: create synthetic tests that mimic 3 typical shapes (short, medium, long) and compare p50/p95/p99 across kernel variants. Add a regression alert rule: if synthetic p95 regresses >30% vs baseline for 15m -> page eng-sre.

sam: Questions: do we want to expose a public status note for transparency? Might help reduce support noise.

jane-support: Yes, short status update on status.redwood.ai: "Investigating increased latency on hosted generate API; mitigation in place, most customers seeing improvement". I'll draft.

alex: Long-term: consider multi-model fallback per-request: attempt fast variant with short timeout and if it doesn't complete forward to robust variant. Similar to hedged requests but cheaper: first try cached/quant variant for 200ms then fallback to full model.

maria: Agreed. Also add deployment guard: do not change kernel-selector without passing a synthetic regression test and a staged rollout with health-check gating on p95.

oncall-bot: ACTIONS LOGGED: rollback applied, circuit-breaker enabled, fallback routing created, autoscaler patch canary.

maria: I'll keep monitoring. If p99 doesn't drop below 700ms in 30m we escalate to SEV.

sam: Thanks everyone, nice coordination. I'll follow up on telemetry dashboard and churn test.

jane-support: I'll keep customers updated and queue affected customers for Dedicated outreach.

ryan: I'll open a postmortem draft with timeline + root cause + remediation playbook. Tagging in the runbook: runbooks/latency-playbook.md

maria: closing loop here, p95 now 150-180ms, p99 ~320ms across regions, still watching. Will post final summary in incident channel when we close INC-20260315-427. :thumbsup:
